title_en: Supreme People's Court Releases Typical Cases on the Blacklist System for Dishonest Judgment Debtors
keywords_en: contract dispute; sales contract; personal injury damages
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court Releases Typical Cases on the List System of Dishonest Persons Subject to Enforcement

Case 1

Zhang v. Henan Mou Food Co., Ltd. — dispute over a sales contract (enforcement case)

(1) Basic Facts

In the dispute over a sales contract between Zhang and Henan Mou Food Industry Co., Ltd., the Huixian City People's Court of Henan Province entered a judgment ordering Henan Mou Food Industry Co., Ltd. to repay Zhang more than RMB 940,000 plus interest.

The case was later designated for enforcement to the Muye District People's Court of Xinxiang City. After the enforcement court served the enforcement notice and the order to report property on the person subject to enforcement, the parties reached a settlement agreement. However, after repaying RMB 200,000 on January 30, 2013, the person subject to enforcement delayed performance on various pretexts. The enforcement court repeatedly urged the legal representative of the person subject to enforcement to continue performing the settlement agreement. The person subject to enforcement repaid RMB 5,000 on May 20, 2013, but thereafter failed to continue performing its obligations.

After the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Publication of Information on the List of Dishonest Persons Subject to Enforcement took effect, the enforcement court issued a decision on October 9, 2013, including Henan Mou Food Industry Co., Ltd. in the list of dishonest persons subject to enforcement, and entered it into the Supreme People's Court's database of the list of dishonest persons subject to enforcement for public disclosure. Under pressure of public opinion and to avoid more serious impact on its commercial reputation, the person subject to enforcement repaid RMB 80,000 in cash and one car to the applying enforcement party on October 15, 2013. Given the considerable difficulty of performing all obligations in one lump sum, the person subject to enforcement voluntarily entered into a settlement agreement with the applying enforcement party to repay RMB 50,000 each month until full satisfaction.

(2) Typical Significance

Publicly disclosing the list information of dishonest persons subject to enforcement to the whole society exposes the dishonesty of the persons subject to enforcement through public publicity, damages their reputation, and forces them to actively perform obligations determined by legal instruments in order to restore their reputation. This achieves the purpose of promoting enforcement and yields good social results. In this case, in order to restore its commercial reputation, the person subject to enforcement voluntarily performed part of its obligations to the applying enforcement party. Although it had difficulty performing all obligations in one lump sum, it actively assumed responsibility and obligations by reaching a settlement agreement with the applying enforcement party and other means.

Case 2

Guo Hongmou v. Guo Shumou — dispute over compensation for personal injury (enforcement case)

(1) Basic Facts

In the dispute over compensation for personal injury brought by Guo Hongmou against Guo Shumou, the Luoyang Intermediate People's Court of Henan Province ordered defendant Guo Shumou to compensate Guo Hongmou for medical expenses, hospital meal subsidies, nutrition expenses, nursing fees, lost wages, disability compensation, and solatium, totaling more than RMB 80,000.

Because Guo Shumou refused to perform the payment obligations determined by the effective judgment, Guo Hongmou applied to the Jianxi District People's Court of Luoyang City for enforcement on January 1, 2012. After opening the case, the enforcement court served the enforcement notice, the order to report property, and other legal instruments on the person subject to enforcement, as well as a risk alert and a letter of commitment to honest litigation, but the person subject to enforcement consistently failed to perform its obligations. The enforcement court repeatedly checked the bank accounts of the person subject to enforcement but found no property available for enforcement. The person subject to enforcement had one property under its name, but to protect the living needs of the person subject to enforcement, the enforcement court could not take compulsory measures. Since the person subject to enforcement had no other property available for enforcement, enforcement of the case was once at an impasse.

The national platform for disclosure and inquiry of information on the list of dishonest persons subject to enforcement of courts was opened to the public on October 24, 2013. Through this platform, the information of dishonest persons subject to enforcement entered by people's courts at all levels across the country could be publicly disclosed, and Guo Shumou was included in the list. Sensing the pressure of public opinion and the risk of credit punishment, Guo Shumou proactively approached the enforcement judge and expressed willingness to cooperate with enforcement. In addition, through the newly established Jianxi District Networked Enforcement Joint Action Command Center, the enforcement court formed joint enforcement links with several entities in the jurisdiction, including industry and commerce, taxation, housing management, land management, and banks, and quickly discovered that Guo Shumou had another property that had been concealed. Upon learning this information, the enforcement judge immediately sealed up the property in accordance with the law and informed Guo Shumou to perform the statutory obligations as soon as possible. Thereafter, Guo Shumou actively cooperated with the court's work and voluntarily paid all the money to the enforcement court.

(2) Typical Significance

This case demonstrates the achievements of the people's courts in information technology construction for enforcement and the construction of a joint enforcement mechanism. The disclosure of the list information of dishonest persons subject to enforcement has effectively deterred dishonest acts and cracked down on various acts that obstruct, resist, or evade enforcement. The enforcement command center has set up a platform for joint enforcement. Through the networked joint enforcement effect, the people's courts can promptly obtain relevant property information of persons subject to enforcement, urge them to perform their obligations, and ensure the smooth conclusion of enforcement cases.

Case 3

Beijing Mou Automobile Decoration Center and over 50 others v. Beijing Mou Automobile Manufacturing Co., Ltd. — series of enforcement cases

(1) Basic Facts

Since 2000, Beijing Mou Automobile Manufacturing Co., Ltd., as the person subject to enforcement, has had a large number of enforcement cases in the Fengtai District People's Court of Beijing, with the amount not yet enforced totaling more than RMB 40 million.

During the enforcement process, the enforcement court sealed up the production line and other property of the person subject to enforcement, Beijing Mou Automobile Manufacturing Co., Ltd. However, because the person subject to enforcement failed to fulfill its custodial duties, some of the sealed property was damaged or lost. According to the appraisal by the Beijing Price Certification Center, the sealed property had lost its conditions for realization. Subsequently, the enforcement court made extensive inquiries but found no bank deposits, vehicles, real estate, or other property available for enforcement under the name of the person subject to enforcement. The legal representative of the person subject to enforcement had been missing for a long time and refused to appear in court to report property. Many applying enforcement parties were very dissatisfied with this.

After the list system of dishonest persons subject to enforcement was introduced, one of the applicants, Beijing Mou Automobile Decoration Center, applied to the enforcement court to include the person subject to enforcement in the list of dishonest persons subject to enforcement. After examination, the enforcement court decided to include the person subject to enforcement in the list on the ground that it had violated the property reporting system, and exposed the information through Jinghua Times, Beijing Youth Daily, Beijing Morning Post, Legal Evening News, The Beijing News, and Beijing Evening News. Subsequently, media such as Beijing Television's "Urban Evening Peak" and "Law in Action", Beijing Radio's "Beijing News", China Court Net, and Beijing Court Net also reported the case, and dozens of websites including People's Net, Xinhua Net, Guangming Net, and Phoenix Net reposted the reports. After seeing the relevant reports, the person subject to enforcement, under the deterrence of the list of dishonest persons subject to enforcement and the pressure of public opinion, voluntarily contacted the enforcement court and sent its authorized attorney to the court to verify the amount of unpaid money, indicating that it would perform its obligations as soon as possible through various means to eliminate the adverse effects. At the same time, the applying enforcement parties, seeing the disclosed information of the dishonest person subject to enforcement in the media, sent a thank-you letter specifically to the enforcement court, expressing understanding of the court's work.

(2) Typical Significance

The enforcement court entered the list information of the dishonest person subject to enforcement into the Supreme People's Court's database of the list of dishonest persons subject to enforcement, publicly disclosed it to the society, and also published it through newspapers, radio, television, the internet, and other means. The person subject to enforcement, as a company, under social pressure and to maintain its reputation in economic dealings, voluntarily expressed to the enforcement court that it would perform its obligations as soon as possible. The credit punishment function of the list system of dishonest persons subject to enforcement was effectively exerted.

Case 4

Zheng Yanmou v. Zheng Qingmou — dispute over a sales contract (enforcement case)

(1) Basic Facts

In the dispute over a sales contract between Zheng Yanmou and Zheng Qingmou, the effective mediation document confirmed that Zheng Qingmou would pay Zheng Yanmou RMB 10,000 on July 19, 2012, the date the mediation agreement was signed, and the remaining amount of RMB 23,930 would be fully paid by December 31, 2012.

However, except for the RMB 10,000 paid at the time of signing the mediation agreement, Zheng Qingmou did not perform the remaining RMB 23,930 in accordance with the agreement. On April 22, 2013, Zheng Yanmou applied to the Zaoqiang County People's Court of Hebei Province for enforcement. After the case entered the enforcement process, the enforcement court served the enforcement notice and the order to report property on the person subject to enforcement in accordance with the law, but the person subject to enforcement neither performed the obligations determined by the mediation document nor reported property to the enforcement court, nor did it appear in court for investigation upon summons. The enforcement court compulsorily deducted RMB 2,400 from the deposit of the person subject to enforcement with the Zaoqiang County Rural Credit Cooperative, but found no other property available for enforcement under the name of the person subject to enforcement. Later, the enforcement court ascertained that the person subject to enforcement had sold a batch of rabbit fur to a certain customer. Therefore, the enforcement court decided to impose judicial detention on the person subject to enforcement on the grounds that it had refused to report property and had the ability to perform but refused to perform the obligations determined by the effective legal instrument.

Subsequently, during the investigation, the enforcement court learned that because the fur market outlook was favorable and the person subject to enforcement was seeking to expand its business, it was in the process of applying for a bank loan and registering a company. In response to the above situation, the enforcement court issued a "Suggestion Letter of Zaoqiang County People's Court on Not Handling Applications of Dishonest Persons Subject to Enforcement" to financial institutions, industry and commerce administration departments, etc. in Zaoqiang County, suggesting that the relevant institutions and departments not handle loan business and company registration for the person subject to enforcement until the case was concluded. On August 20, 2013, Zheng Qingmou, the person subject to enforcement, came to the enforcement court, stating that because of his dishonest conduct, the bank refused to grant him a loan, and the industry and commerce department had stopped processing his company registration. The person subject to enforcement expressed willingness to voluntarily perform the obligations determined by the civil mediation document and requested the people's court to delete his name from the list of dishonest persons subject to enforcement. On August 22 of the same year, the parties reached a settlement agreement, whereby Zheng Qingmou paid Zheng Yanmou RMB 20,000 in a lump sum for the goods price (including the amount compulsorily deducted by the enforcement court from the credit cooperative), and Zheng Yanmou voluntarily waived the remaining amount. This case was finally concluded smoothly.

(2) Typical Significance

Providing targeted notification of list information of dishonest persons subject of enforcement to relevant units, which then impose credit sanctions on dishonest persons subject to enforcement in areas such as government procurement, bidding, administrative approval, government support, financing credit, market access, and qualification recognition, is an important channel for the list system of dishonest persons subject to enforcement to function and produce effects. In this case, because the person subject to enforcement was restricted in obtaining loans, establishing companies, etc., which prevented it from carrying out business activities and squeezed its social living space, it voluntarily performed its obligations to the enforcement court.

Case 5

Li v. Yang — dispute over a loan contract (enforcement case)

(1) Basic Facts

In the dispute over a loan contract between Li and Yang, the Wuhua District People's Court of Kunming, Yunnan Province entered a judgment ordering Li to repay Yang principal and interest in the amount of RMB 1,340,547.

After the judgment took effect, Li failed to voluntarily perform the obligations determined by the legal instrument. Yang then applied to the Wuhua District People's Court of Kunming, Yunnan Province for compulsory enforcement on September 5, 2013. During the enforcement process, the enforcement court sealed up and froze the real estate and equity interests under the name of Li, the person subject to enforcement, in accordance with the law, and informed Li that if he failed to timely perform the obligations determined by the effective legal instrument, the enforcement court would strictly follow the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Publication of Information on the List of Dishonest Persons Subject to Enforcement and include him in the list of dishonest persons subject to enforcement. Once publicly disclosed, this would have a significant impact on the person subject to enforcement's travel, credit, business activities, and family life. Upon learning of this legal consequence, Li, who was in the process of applying for a visa to go abroad, in order to avoid adverse effects on his future travel abroad or exit from the country, raised funds from various sources during the National Day holiday. On the first day after the holiday ended, he voluntarily approached the enforcement court and fully performed the obligations determined by the effective legal instrument.

(2) Typical Significance

In this case, while taking compulsory measures such as sealing up and freezing in accordance with the law, the enforcement court informed the person subject to enforcement of the risk of being included in the list of dishonest persons subject to enforcement, making him feel pressure from daily life, business dealings, and other aspects. This ultimately prompted the person subject to enforcement to voluntarily perform the obligations determined by the effective legal instrument. The deterrence function of the list system of dishonest persons subject to enforcement was effectively exerted, highlighting judicial authority.
